questionReviews.blindDerivation: Cube root of 250 is 5*cuberoot(2); sqrt(cuberoot(4)) is cuberoot(2). Hence 5-a=2 and a=3.
Combining common logarithms gives log((x/5)*(9/6))=log(12); therefore 3x/10=12 and x=40.
For t<0, the principal even roots give A=|t|=-t and B=sqrt(t^2)=|t|=-t, whereas C=t^(4*(1/4))=t.
For radius r and central angle 2π/3, sector area S=rl/2. The condition S=9l yields r=18, so l=r*(2π/3)=12π.
The argument is positive for 1<x<9. The base 8-x must be positive and unequal to 1, giving x<8 and x≠7. Allowed integers are 2,3,4,5,6, whose sum is 20.

In 3π/4<θ<π, sine is positive and cosine negative, with |cos θ|>|sin θ|. Using (sin θ-cos θ)^2=1-2sin θ cos θ=(17/13)^2 gives sin θ cos θ=-60/169. The compatible pair is sin θ=5/13, cos θ=-12/13, so tan θ=-5/12.
Divide 2xy+xz-yz=xyz by xyz to obtain 2/z+1/y-1/x=1. From common k, 1/x=log_k 4, 1/y=log_k 9 and 1/z=log_k 6. Thus log_k(6^2*9/4)=1, so k=81 and log_3 k=4.

questionReviews.blindAnswer: The statement that the graph passes through (7,4) is false.
questionReviews.blindDerivation: The asymptote gives a=3, and f(5)=2 gives b=1. Hence f(x)=log_2(x-3)+1, and f(7)=log_2 4+1=3, not 4. The other four statements hold.
Subtracting the two decibel equations gives 65-35=10 log(I_1/I_2), so log(I_1/I_2)=3 and I_1/I_2=10^3.
Write r=log_a b>1. Then r+1/r=3 gives r=(3+√5)/2. The requested logarithm equals (2+r)/(1+r)=(15-√5)/10.
Put u=2^x+2^(-x)≥2. Then f=u^2-6u+7=(u-3)^2-2. At u=3 the minimum is m=-2 and 2^p+2^(-p)=3, making the requested sum 1.
Since g is inverse to f, f(3)=2 and f(27)=5. Thus k+p=2 and 3k+p=5, yielding k=3/2, p=1/2. The equation f(x)=8 gives log_3 x=5, so g(8)=3^5=243.

questionReviews.blindAnswer: The claimed smallest positive asymptote x=π/6 is false.
questionReviews.blindDerivation: For tan(3x+π/6), the vertical asymptotes satisfy 3x+π/6=π/2+kπ, i.e. x=π/9+kπ/3. The smallest positive one is π/9, not π/6. The other claims check out.

f(x)=-(x-3)^2+10 has maximum 10 on [0,5]. Since log_2 is increasing, M=log_2(10+7)=log_2 17. Since log_(1/3) is decreasing, m=log_(1/3)(10+6)=-log_3 16. Their product is -log_2 17*log_3 16=-4log_3 17.
Putting y=1-x into x^2+y^2=13 gives (x-3)(x+2)=0. Hence P=(-2,3) in quadrant II and Q=(3,-2) in quadrant IV. Both sin θ_1 and cos θ_2 equal 3/√13, so their sum is 6√13/13.

The circle is x^2+(y-4)^2=4, with center distance 4 and radius 2. Its origin distances OP cover [2,6]. For 2^(OP/2) to be a natural number, its integer value must be 2,3,4,5,6,7 or 8. Distances 2 and 6 occur at one point each; each of the other five distances at two points, totaling 1+5*2+1=12.

The student-facing graph has centerline y=1, maximum 4, minimum -2, consecutive maxima at x=-π/18 and x=11π/18, and minimum at x=5π/18. The negative amplitude is a=-3. Peak separation is 2π/3, so b=3. Since the negative-amplitude sine has a minimum when bx-c=π/2 modulo 2π, at x=5π/18 we get 5π/6-c=π/2, hence c=π/3 (the permitted 0<c<π). Therefore abc=(-3)*3*(π/3)=-3π.

At y=0 the two x-coordinates are 3±1/2, separated by 1. At y=k the two x-coordinates are 3±2^(k-1), separated by 2^k. These are horizontal parallel sides of a trapezoid of height k, with area k(1+2^k)/2=27/2. The positive integer solution is k=3.

A fourth-quadrant crossing must have 0<x<n/2 and sin(πx/2)>0, placing x in positive sine lobes (4j,4j+2). On each full such lobe before n/2, the concave sine arch intersects the descending line 1-2x/n twice; on a lobe truncated at or before its right zero, there is just one crossing. Exactly three fourth-quadrant intersections therefore occur when the first lobe (0,2) is full and the second (4,6) is truncated: 4<n/2≤6, equivalently 8<n≤12. Hence n=9,10,11,12 and their sum is 42. Endpoint x=6 for n=12 lies on the x-axis, not in quadrant IV.
A clockwise rotation through 390 degrees is -390°=-13π/6, coterminal with -π/6 and 11π/6. Add 2kπ for every integer k. Its terminal side lies 30° below the positive x-axis, in the fourth quadrant.

Use sin(π+θ)=-sin θ and cos(π-θ)=-cos θ. The quadratic in x becomes x^2-2√2 sin θ*x+1-cos θ. Strict positivity for every real x requires discriminant <0: 8sin²θ-4(1-cos θ)<0. With t=cos θ, this is 2t²-t-1>0, i.e. (2t+1)(t-1)>0. Since -1≤t≤1, it means cos θ<-1/2. Under 0<θ<2π this is 2π/3<θ<4π/3. Tangent on this entire interval ranges strictly between -√3 and √3, attaining 0 at θ=π.

For odd n in {3,5,7,9,11}, an odd-degree equation t^n=A always has exactly one real solution, contributing 5. For even n in {2,4,6,8,10,12}, A=-(n-4)(n-10): negative for n=2,12, zero for n=4,10, positive for n=6,8. Even-root counts are respectively 0,1,2,2,1,0, totaling 6. Thus the sum is 11.

On x<-2, f=-x-1 ranges over (1,∞), excluding its limiting point (-2,1). On x≥-2, f=|2^(1-x)-4| starts at (-2,4), decreases to (-1,0), then increases toward the nonattained horizontal asymptote y=4. Thus for integers n∈[-8,8], g(n)=0 on {-8,...,-1} (8 values), g(n)=1 on {0,5,6,7,8} (5 values), g(n)=2 on {1,4} (2 values), and g(n)=3 on {2,3} (2 values). To sum to 3, the ordered g-values must be (0,3),(3,0),(1,2),(2,1), yielding 8*2+2*8+5*2+2*5=52.
